items.question: What future research directions do the authors of the network embedding method plan to investigate beyond first-order and second-order proximities?
items.gold_answer: The authors plan to investigate higher-order proximity beyond the first-order and second-order proximities in the network. They also plan to study embeddings for heterogeneous information networks, including vertices with multiple types.
items.evidence_quote: In the future, we plan to investigate higher-order proximity beyond the first-order and second-order proximities in the network.

items.question: How do the authors of the network embedding method describe their plans for handling heterogeneous information networks?
items.gold_answer: They say they plan to investigate the embedding of heterogeneous information networks. In particular, they mention networks with vertices that have multiple types.
items.evidence_quote: Besides, we also plan to investigate the embedding of heterogeneous information networks, e.g., vertices with multiple types.

items.question: Under which kinds of network properties do the authors of the network embedding method say they will extend their work in the future?
items.gold_answer: They intend to extend their work to higher-order proximity and to heterogeneous information networks. These directions go beyond the first-order and second-order proximities already discussed and include vertices with multiple types.
items.evidence_quote: In the future, we plan to investigate higher-order proximity beyond the first-order and second-order proximities in the network.

items.question: What specific example of heterogeneity do the authors of the network embedding method give when describing future work, and what does that imply about the network setting?
items.gold_answer: They give the example of vertices with multiple types. This implies they want to study embeddings in heterogeneous information networks where nodes may not all belong to the same type.
items.evidence_quote: Besides, we also plan to investigate the embedding of heterogeneous information networks, e.g., vertices with multiple types.
